scope_note: Second corrective evidence and model-input audit for the selected 315,400-square-foot IM3 building footprint at Meta's Altoona campus in Polk County. project_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — selected building remains distinct from campus
project_updates.notes: The inventory target is one 315,400-square-foot building footprint named Facebook Altoona Data Center 1, while operator, IEDA, city, tax and DNR sources overwhelmingly describe the multi-building Siculus/Meta Altoona campus. Facebook announced the project April 23, 2013 and reported the Altoona data center online November 14, 2014. Assessor PIN 792310401005 contains ATN1, ATN2, ATN3, ATN4, ATN-4B and security sections; ATN1 is 312,131 square feet, close to but not equal to the IM3 footprint. It is retained only as a candidate crosswalk, so every campus, parcel and company-county amount remains unallocated. Siculus is a Facebook subsidiary and Facebook's corporate rename to Meta is operator continuity, not a predecessor transfer.
project_updates.project_description: Meta's Altoona project is an operating multi-building data-center campus in Altoona, Polk County, Iowa, held in public records through its Siculus subsidiary. Facebook announced the project in April 2013 and reported the data center online on November 14, 2014; subsequent expansions extended construction into the 2020s. This account follows the selected 315,400-square-foot IM3 building footprint while keeping campus-wide investment, employment, utility, permit, incentive, and community figures unallocated from that building.

project_updates.title: Utility and infrastructure audit — tariff and franchise models tested, bills absent
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Altoona utility, council-minutes and code records, infrastructure and will-serve amendments, water/sewer materials, MidAmerican's filed Iowa tariffs, and Siculus/Meta meter, demand, electricity, franchise-fee, pump-station and reimbursement paths. Meta's actual 2020-2024 kWh deterministically convert to annual average load of 111.872146, 108.527968, 119.133105, 141.929909 and 180.486339 MW (2024 uses 8,784 hours); those conversions are retained separately in modeled synthesis. MidAmerican offers materially different Large General Service, Substation Service and Individual Customer Rate structures, with demand, voltage, ratchet, rider, curtailment and possible special-contract terms. Average demand is a lower bound on peak billing demand but supplies no finite upper bound; therefore neither total electricity expense nor the associated franchise-fee base is bounded by annual kWh. Indispensable missing inputs are the service tariff/class or contract, monthly interval/billed kW, voltage and meter count, power factor, riders, bill totals, and customer-specific franchise inclusion, exemption/credit and remittance records. No tariff-cost or franchise-fee estimate is retained. The $500,000 pump-station commitment remains prospective because no completion, invoice or payment record was found.

project_updates.title: Environmental audit — permitted equipment and resource observations kept distinct
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Iowa DNR Facility Explorer operating site 310199764, construction site 312068167, Title V permit 18-TV-007R1, NPDES General Permit No. 2 index, Polk County air-source listings, Meta environmental data, and exact facility/address/entity queries. The final air permit supports 112 permitted emergency engines across ATN and PCI groups; no engine is allocated to the selected building and permit limits are not actual emissions or generation. Meta reports annual Altoona electricity and water withdrawals for 2020-2024. Electricity is normalized directly; water values of 151, 140, 199, 173 and 242 megaliters remain documented here because the governed dictionary lacks an actual-water metric. No site-specific discharge, fuel-use, actual-emissions, generator-run-hour, water-payment, wastewater-payment, or construction-water allocation was found.

project_updates.title: Workforce, procurement and supplier audit — hours and contractor identities found, spend absent
project_updates.notes: The reopened workforce and supplier trail covered Turner, IES Communications, Allied Construction Services, City permit reports, bid and procurement indexes, claims/check-register and lien queries, Hardhat in Hand/DMACC training, and recipient records. Meta names Turner, reports seven training graduates, and reports 8.7 million construction work hours since 2013; Iowa WARN identifies an IES event at 500 Share Way, and OSHA identifies Allied at 100 Share Way. Dividing 8.7 million hours by a 2,080-hour convention yields 4,182.692307692308 standardized FTE-year equivalents, retained only as labor-time equivalence—not unique workers, observed FTE, Iowa-resident employment or a selected-building result. Applying IEDA's $23.12 and $53.87 qualifying-job wage commitments yields $201.144 million and $468.669 million, with a $334.9065 million midpoint; this is retained as benchmark sensitivity, not observed payroll or a statistical/true-value bound. A 400-person operating scenario times 2,080 hours and the same wage anchors yields $19.23584 million, $32.02784 million midpoint and $44.81984 million, also retained only as sensitivity because daily people are not annual FTEs and may mix employees/contractors. Indispensable inputs remain certified payroll, trade/hour distributions, annual average employee and contractor FTE, benefits, residence, occupation mix, supplier invoices and local-purchase shares. Supplier contribution remains unsupported; payroll scenarios are modeled separately with all limitations.

project_updates.title: Community and recipient audit — direct funding retained with overlap controls
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Meta Altoona grants/sponsorship statements and Community Action Grant recipient pages, Altoona local archives, Iowa State University Extension Polk County, schools and nonprofits, using grant, donation, sponsorship, recipient and amount queries. The operator reports more than $2.6 million cumulatively through December 2021; a local 2015 announcement identifies $103,000 to 25 nonprofits and schools, and ISU Extension independently confirms a Meta-supported STEM event but gives no amount. The 2015 amount is nested within the cumulative total and must not be summed. No complete annual ledger, recipient-level reconciliation, in-kind valuation, volunteer-hour value, or causal outcome measurement was found.

project_updates.title: Expansion, adjacent project and continuity audit — phases kept separate
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: operator announcements from 2013-2026, local permit reports, DNR ATN/PCI equipment labels, Siculus corporate identity, and reporting for adjacent Polk County data-center construction. Operator sources describe at least seven expansions and a campus expected to exceed five million square feet; permit records specifically identify later ATN 5/6 work. No evidence supports treating all later buildings, adjacent confidential projects, regional wind generation, or every Siculus parcel as the selected original building. Corporate sources support Facebook-to-Meta/Siculus continuity, so no predecessor asset transfer or pre-acquisition baseline is inferred.

project_updates.title: Fiscal and public-cost audit — real-property payments found; net account still unbounded
project_updates.notes: The correction establishes separate actual 2020-2024 real-property payment series for all 10 active Siculus PINs plus current taxable values and bills. Exact annual active-PIN sums are $1,321,478, $1,834,994, $1,846,260, $2,219,356 and $2,249,854; they are retained as modeled aggregation totals with all retired/successor terminal bills excluded and may not be added to component claims. The 2024 $2,249,854 total also defines the equal-cost annual local-service break-even threshold. That threshold is not observed cost or net fiscal benefit; missing PILOT, franchise, incentive-realization and public-cost series are the reason to publish the threshold, not a reason to omit it. The approximately $810,000 temporary-building PILOT remains a projection with no receipt; the $500,000 pump-station commitment has no completion/payment record; IEDA's $26 million maximum remains a ceiling; and the reported 2019 PILOT/abatement/franchise terms lack a realized city ledger. Exact Siculus/Facebook/Meta searches found no named row among 332 Altoona TIF-expenditure or 475 Altoona urban-renewal rows, which does not prove zero unnamed or non-TIF cost. No realized public-service-cost dollar record or net fiscal result is asserted.

project_updates.title: County-statistics audit — two treatment dates and a screened Iowa donor pool tested
project_updates.notes: The governed 2001-2024 BLS QCEW employment/wage and BEA GDP panel was tested with construction-start treatment in 2013 and first-operation treatment in 2014. The candidate untreated pool is Linn, Johnson, Scott, Black Hawk, Woodbury, Dubuque and Story counties; Dallas and Pottawattamie were excluded for known hyperscale data-center exposure. The pool is explicit but not pre-registered, and Polk had Microsoft exposure by 2012 while Meta construction and later phases overlap. Results are retained only as design diagnostics, not contribution estimates.

project_updates.title: County outcome model decisions — pretrend, donor and treatment sensitivity tested separately
project_updates.notes: Using the seven-county unweighted pool and 2001-2012 preperiod, normalized-log-index RMSE / annual-growth correlation / pre-gap slope were: employment 0.0182 / 0.890 / -0.320% per year; nominal weekly wage 0.0245 / 0.648 / +0.008% per year; real GDP 0.0519 / 0.705 / -0.859% per year. Mean 2013-2019 post-versus-pre gaps were employment +2.547638%, wage -0.387495%, GDP +7.450688%; switching treatment to 2014 produced +3.099642%, -0.402464% and +10.169728%. Leave-one-donor-out ranges across both treatment specifications were employment +1.979955% to +4.260418%, wage -0.833174% to +0.111288%, and GDP +4.860594% to +13.547587%. Employment has good raw prefit but a nonflat pre-gap and overlapping 2013 construction/2014 operations/later expansions; GDP has weaker prefit, a material pretrend and treatment sensitivity; wage has a nearly flat pre-gap and a robust near-zero descriptive result, but county average composition, concurrent metro treatments and absent selected-building exposure prevent project attribution. Each diagnostic is retained as a low-confidence descriptive comparison-gap sensitivity, never as a Meta effect, causal result or selected-building contribution.

project_updates.title: Contribution-account disposition — second corrective candidate pending adversarial review
project_updates.notes: The second-corrected evidence fragment contains 100 records: 91 reported actuals and nine source projections, including two explicit IEDA qualifying-wage inputs. Together with the one existing baseline construction-peak record, the merged project has 101 direct records, 92 reported actuals and nine projections. The new modeled-synthesis fragment contains 17 estimates: five exact annual active-PIN tax aggregations, one 2024 equal-cost local-service threshold, five deterministic average-load conversions, one construction job-year equivalence, two payroll sensitivities and three descriptive county comparison gaps. All remain unallocated or not applicable to the selected building; aggregation notes prohibit adding modeled totals to component claims. Material gaps remain for selected-building allocation, personal property, ordinary tax distributions, PILOT/franchise receipts, realized incentives, audited payroll, supplier/local spending, observed public costs, tariff bills and causal county outcomes. The five exact water observations have a complete proposed metric/record/regression payload for orchestrator catalog reconciliation. This handoff supersedes both earlier zero-model conclusions, is candidate_corrected_round2_pending_adversarial_review, and is not accepted evidence.
